name: ADHD Guard
subtitle: Focus reminders for your Mac
promotional_text: A quick detour can turn into a lost hour. Choose your focus apps and distracting sites, and let ADHD Guard remind you to get back to what matters.
description:
Get back to what matters.

You open a tab for a quick break. You switch apps to check one thing. ADHD Guard helps you notice when that detour takes you away from your task.

Choose your focus apps and distracting websites, then turn on Focus mode. If you stay outside your focus apps or on a distracting site beyond your chosen buffer, a visible reminder prompts you to return. Optional sound and spoken reminders keep nudging you until you get back to focus.

CHOOSE YOUR FOCUS APPS
Build a list of the apps you want to work in. Add apps from recent activity or choose them from your Applications folder.

CATCH YOUR DISTRACTING SITES
Add the websites that tend to pull you away. Listed sites start the reminder timer even when your browser is a focus app. Matching subdomains are included.

GIVE YOURSELF A MOMENT
Set how long a detour can last before reminders begin. Switching between distracting apps and sites keeps the same timer running.

RETURN TO YOUR TASK
Use Return to focus to bring your last focused app or browser page back into view. Move the reminder banner to a spot that suits your workspace.

MAKE REMINDERS YOUR OWN
Choose a repeating chime, spoken reminders, or a visual reminder on its own. Write your own reminder phrases and preview them in Settings. Enable an optional idle reminder for periods without keyboard or mouse activity.

KEEP IT CLOSE
Turn Focus mode on or off from the menu bar, check recent activity, and choose to launch ADHD Guard when you log in.

YOUR ACTIVITY STAYS LOCAL
Focus rules, reminder settings, and a short recent activity list are stored on your Mac. The app does not upload your app or browsing activity. No account is required.

Website reminders work with Safari and Google Chrome and require macOS Automation permission.

For work, study, and the moments when you could use a reminder to come back.

Support: kp.gentle.support@gmail.com
review_notes:
ADHD Guard is a macOS productivity app that displays reminders when the active app is outside the user's focus list or the active browser tab matches a distracting website rule.

No account or sign-in is required. No demo credentials are needed.

To test an app reminder:
1. Open Lists > Focus apps and add TextEdit using Choose an application.
2. Open Settings and set Focus buffer to 10 seconds. Leave Idle reminder off for this test. Chime and Spoken reminder can be enabled or disabled independently.
3. Turn on Focus mode.
4. Use TextEdit briefly so that it becomes the last focused app.
5. Open Calculator, ensuring Calculator is not in the focus list, and keep it frontmost for more than 10 seconds.
6. A Time to refocus banner appears. Select Return to focus to return to TextEdit. The distraction reminder clears when focus resumes.

To test a website reminder:
1. Keep Safari in the focus-app list.
2. Under Lists > Distracting sites, add example.org.
3. Open a non-listed page such as apple.com in Safari to establish a focused page.
4. Allow macOS Automation access when prompted.
5. Open example.org and keep its tab active beyond the configured buffer.
6. The reminder should appear even though Safari itself is a focus app. Return to focus selects the previous focused browser page; if the matching tab is no longer open, the app can reopen the saved URL.
7. Turn Focus mode off to stop reminders. Recent activity still updates locally while the app is running.

Browser website detection uses Apple Events and requires the user's macOS Automation consent. Safari and Google Chrome are suitable browsers for the review scenario. App-based reminders can be tested independently of browser permission.

The build uses App Sandbox. The temporary Apple Events exception is restricted to Safari, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave and Arc. It supports reading the active tab URL to evaluate local rules and searching open tab URLs when the user explicitly chooses to return to a saved website.

No screen recording, Accessibility, microphone or full-disk access is requested. The app reads elapsed time since input events for optional idle reminders; it does not capture typed text. Selected application bundles are read only to obtain their names and bundle identifiers. Rules, preferences and a short recent activity list are stored locally. The app does not upload activity.
sandbox_justification:
ADHD Guard uses com.apple.security.temporary-exception.apple-events for these specific browser targets: com.apple.Safari, com.google.Chrome, com.microsoft.edgemac, com.brave.Browser and company.thebrowser.Browser.

Website-based reminders need the URL of the current tab in the frontmost supported browser to compare its host against the user's local distracting-site rules. App identity alone cannot distinguish a focused page from a distracting website in the same browser.

When the user explicitly selects Return to focus or a saved website, ADHD Guard searches the supported browser's open tab URLs for the saved URL and activates the matching tab. If it cannot find a matching tab, it can ask the browser to open the saved URL.

The app does not read page contents, browser passwords or the browser history database, and does not change website content. Browser access requires macOS Automation consent. The exception targets are limited to the browsers implemented by the app; it does not grant unrestricted Apple Events access.

URLs used for recent activity and focus return are handled locally. The app does not upload app or browsing activity.
